Of the 26.5 pts who had used by 2030, 19.9 are on and 6.6 are off. On: 8.0 + 19.9 = 27.9. Off: 2.5 + 6.6 = 9.1. Within the 2030 cohort: 11.3 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (60%, up from ~50% in 2028–30 because conditional coverage penalises stopping and the price fell). The 7.5 who stopped joined the 7.7 already off, making a pool of 15.2. Of those, 8.6 restarted (57% over two years, in line with the parent's 55%), so 11.3 + 8.6 = 19.9 on and 15.2 − 8.6 = 6.6 off. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030, plus ~4.0 pts of first-time restarters in the 2030 cohort and ~0.5 among new starters, give 13.4 of 37.0 ever-users = 36%. Current users ≈ 74.8M of ~268M adults. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.2 + 10.23 + 10.56 + 3.91 = 27.9. Income thirds: (34 + 28 + 21.7)/3 = 27.9. The 18–29 band rose most in relative terms (10→16) through the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program, police and fire contracts, and cheaper oral starts. The 65+ band rose only 12→17 (~10.5M) despite the dementia-risk label, because the bone wave and Bridge DEXA conditions slowed it. Bottom-third use reached 21.7% through conditioned Medicaid, HRSA free provision and $149 oral starts, and remains mostly lower-efficacy product. Off-drug: ~24.4M adults have used and stopped, many of them cut off by conditioning rules (missed weigh-ins, lack of BMI progress) rather than by choice. ~169M have never used: a mix of deliberate refusers, now an organised constituency, the uninsured in non-expansion states, and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, of whom ~150k are aged 6–11. The first registry bone data arrived in 2032 (see ledger). A cohort of children has now grown up eating at tables where at least one parent is on a drug.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was renewed in Dec 2031 through 2033. Payment falls from $275 to $225/month from Jan 2032 under the Strategic Supply Agreement pricing. The copay stays $50. Continuation is now conditional: ≥5% weight loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and for 65+ a baseline and annual DEXA plus a documented resistance-training referral. About 3.4M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 3.4M × $225 × 12 ≈ $9.2B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈14.7% of incretin fills ≈ 11.0M users (≈10.5M adults 65+ plus ~0.5M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈12% ≈ 9.0M users at $225: 9.0M × $225 × 12 ≈ $24.3B/yr combined federal and state. Seven states run Indiana-style adherence waivers: Indiana and Arkansas, plus Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio and Montana. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program received $5.0B in FY2032 and is still unconditional (refill pickup only). It serves ≈3.6M: 2.4M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $2.0B, plus 1.2M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $179 × 12 = $2.6B, ≈ $4.6B. TRICARE, the VA and the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program cover ≈2.4M, including ~140k active-duty members in the readiness programme: 140k × $149 federal price × 12 ≈ $250M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $7–40/month, and generic tirzepatide has launched in India, Brazil and Turkey. Generic semaglutide is sold across Canada, Mexico, China and most of Latin America and Asia. Chinese originator triple agonists are approved domestically by the NMPA. US generic semaglutide entry dates are set by patent settlements for 2033. Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~74.8M users: commercial 38.5% (28.8M), Medicare 14.7% (11.0M), Medicaid 12% (9.0M), HRSA free 4.8% (3.6M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.2% (2.4M), cash/direct 14.8% (11.1M), gray 12% (9.0M) = 100%. Managed decline: the March 2031 Strategic Supply Agreement and Novo's matching deal stepped TrumpRx/direct prices down to $249 (semaglutide injection), $299 (tirzepatide), $149 (oral starting doses: Wegovy pill, Foundayo) and $399 (retatrutide, newly unallocated). Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Almost nobody pays list. Coverage is the rationing tool. Employer weight-management coverage rose from 57% to 63%, but ~55% of covering employers now attach conditions: PBM-verified ≥80% PDC, ≥5% loss at 6 months, and coaching enrollment. Some add premium differentials of up to 30% under the 2031 tri-agency outcomes-based wellness guidance, which accepts PBM adherence data as a 'reasonable alternative standard'. Gray users are flat at ~9M in absolute terms. Expanded Section 232 duties and CBP seizure of Indian mail pens squeezed imports, but 503A 'personalised' compounders ($99–199) switched part of their API sourcing. Research-peptide retatrutide shrank once the branded product hit $399. Conditioning has produced a 'skip-but-fill' pattern: users pick up refills to keep PDC above 80% while taking dose holidays, which degrades adherence data as a clinical signal.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver realised through an existing product in a new form: FDA approved a retatrutide 12 mg maintenance dose in Jun 2031 on TRIUMPH-4 extension data (30.4% mean loss at 104 weeks in the efficacy estimand). Lilly's new Virginia API plant then lifted allocation. MariTide (BLA Jul 2030) was approved Sep 2031 with limited launch supply, ~0.6M users. Survodutide, resubmitted after its 2029 CRL, was approved Nov 2031 narrowly for obesity with MASH F2–F3. Amycretin was resubmitted in 2031 after Novo's facility remediation and is under review, with a decision in 2033. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (phase 3) filed a BLA in Mar 2032 under muscle-wave pressure; it is not on the market and the decision is not before 2033. The dementia label rests on a confirmatory randomised prevention trial in metabolic-risk adults (HR ~0.82 for all-cause dementia, weighted toward vascular and mixed dementia) and adjudicated SELECT/SOUL follow-up. The 2025 EVOKE failure in established Alzheimer's still stands, and the label says so. The incretin market is ≈$165B globally in 2032: US volume +49% and US net price −15 to −20%.

food_and_beverage.state: With more than one adult in four on drug, US packaged-food volume falls ~2.5% a year. Snacks and confectionery are hit hardest. Majors finish selling indulgent brands to private equity and regional owners. Protein, fibre and now 'bone-and-muscle' formats (calcium, leucine, vitamin D) grow, sold as companions to Bridge counselling.

alcohol.state: AUD coverage plus a quarter of adults on appetite-reducing drugs keep US spirits and beer volume falling for a fourth year. Distillers lean on exports and premium single-serve formats. State excise forecasts now carry an explicit incretin line.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fast casual sells 'half plates' at near-full price. Military-town restaurants near Fort Bragg and Fort Hood report smaller checks. Church-hall potlucks and 'open table' suppers from the backlash movement are a small countercurrent with no measurable effect on sales.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening. Workwear and uniform makers re-cut for leaner police and military bodies. Hip-protector and fall-safe apparel enters mainstream senior catalogues.

fitness.state: Resistance training is now prescribed. Bridge referrals and employer conditions feed low-cost gyms, physical-therapy chains and Medicare Advantage strength programmes. The research-peptide gym trade shrinks as branded retatrutide gets cheaper.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+9% as net prices fall and volume rises. Plans manage cost through conditions rather than exclusions: adherence gates, BMI-progress gates and premium differentials. PBMs sell adherence-verification as a service. Litigation over wellness differentials is pending in two circuits.

pharma.state: Lilly is the designated national champion: tariff-exempt, DPA-financed, and the federal price setter. Novo matches on price and absorbs tariff on Danish API, so margin compresses. Generic liraglutide makers hold HRSA contracts. US exposure to Indian API is now a board-level risk at compounders. MDL reserves are rising.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now carries a payer's conditions as well as a molecule. A lean body with muscle and a DEXA history reads as compliant: Bridge-renewed, employer-qualified, tape-passed. A heavier body reads three ways: cut off by a missed condition, priced out, or refusing on principle. The last is now a public identity, not an excuse.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' has spread down-market as retatrutide fell to $399, so muscle has become the marker. Retatrutide without training produces thin, soft bodies, and coaches call it 'pen-thin'. Among women 65+ in Sun City, Arizona, the visible class marker is posture and a fall-free year: the affluent buy antiresorptives, protein and twice-weekly trainers; others get a referral slip.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: A counter-ritual has formed. 'Open Table' suppers, started in Grand Rapids church networks and copied in Nashville and Tulsa, frame shared full meals as fellowship against 'pharmaceutical fasting'. Fat-liberation groups in Oakland and Brooklyn run 'unmedicated' supper clubs. Family-doctor guidance on 'kid portions' now includes children watching parents skip meals.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule, and some list 'drug-free since 2029' as a value, not a confession. Couples where one partner is on a conditioned employer plan negotiate dose holidays around the plan's adherence window.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical and, through coverage, contractual. The backlash reclaims it as moral or sacred: 'hunger is how we were made' is a sermon line and a bumper sticker. Two states (Tennessee, Idaho) passed laws barring employers from conditioning premiums on incretin use, framed as 'appetite liberty'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Validated retatrutide data (Apr 2031) put clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~8% vs ~4% at high doses. Across agents ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure. About 45% of long-term users report at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year, and conditional coverage pushes many of these into 'skip-but-fill'. Low-dose Foundayo for BED (approved Jun 2032) had ~0.9M users by year-end, inside the commercial and cash shares. Telehealth wellness 'quiet' subscriptions fell from ~2M to ~1.3M as the FTC acted and the complaint went mainstream.
interior_life.framing: A complaint and a treatment at once. 'The grey' is everyday vocabulary, and late-night monologues joke about it. Pharmacists ask 'are you holidaying this month?' The same effect is advertised for BED as 'quiet the noise around food'. Clinicians say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. The backlash says 'chemical contentment'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers have stopped marketing 'focus' perks after the FTC and union pushback. Conditioned benefit plans still make adherence a workplace variable. Sales staff time holidays to quarter-end. Military and police programmes track tape, weight and DEXA, not mood, though Army chaplains report soldiers describing 'the grey' at counselling.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is now a common billing, not a niche one, and some festivals sell 'holiday weekend' passes timed to when users skip. Comedy built on the grey is a genre. Sports-betting and casino operators cite reduced handle in earnings calls again.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Dose holidays around anniversaries and conception attempts are routine. Sex therapists now cite the retatrutide label section directly. Partners on mismatched conditioned plans argue over whose adherence window governs the holiday.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Two blocs cut across party. Pro-access populists defend TrumpRx prices and readiness programmes. An anti-pharma, religious and fat-liberation coalition opposes conditioning, the military programme and 'calm marketing'. Candidates are asked if they are on, and lately whether they take holidays. Turnout effects are still unmeasured.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and price-managing. It approves new indications (BED, dementia risk, MASH) and new forms (retatrutide 12 mg, MariTide), and acts on bone and muscle through labelling rather than restriction. Gray-market enforcement has shifted from letters to customs seizures and one indictment.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Subsidy channels: the Medicare Bridge ($225/$50, conditional), the HRSA programme ($5.0B FY2032, unconditional), the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program, and the ACA cessation mandate (two 90-day courses a year). The Strategic Supply Agreement ties federal prices to Lilly's tariff exemption.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is now the dominant access tool. Seven Medicaid adherence waivers. Bridge continuation tied to 6-month response, PDC and DEXA. Employer outcomes-based wellness plans use PBM adherence feeds and premium differentials. Tennessee and Idaho ban premium conditioning. HRSA remains the unconditioned exception, and plaintiffs and critics cite it from both sides.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program (May 2031) offers tirzepatide or semaglutide through military treatment facilities to service members who fail body-composition standards: ~140k active duty, plus Guard pilots. Body-composition failure separations fell ~30% in FY2032. The FAA streamlined special issuance for pilots on stable doses. Big-city police and fire contracts (Phoenix, Houston, Chicago) cover drugs for fitness-standard compliance. DOT apnea clearance still runs through tirzepatide. About 1,900 religious-accommodation requests to decline the readiness programme have been filed. Participation is formally voluntary, but separation for failing standards is not.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Incretins are designated critical medicines under Section 232 Phase II (Mar 2031), with duties extended to API and peptide intermediates. Lilly is the national champion, with tariff exemption and Defense Production Act Title III financing for its Virginia and Texas plants in return for federal ceiling prices and priority supply to DoD and VA. Novo pays duty on Danish API amid broader US–Denmark friction. India's mail exports are seized at the border, and India files a WTO consultation request. Chinese controls on protected amino-acid exports (Aug 2031) raised compounder costs. Global South markets run on Indian generics.

open_tensions: The dementia-risk label pulls older adults onto the drug just as the bone wave makes them the group it harms most visibly. Medicare now pays for both the incretin and the antiresorptive, and nobody has trial data on the combination's fracture outcome in 75+.

Conditional coverage depends on adherence data, while dose holidays for the mainstream 'grey' complaint push users into skip-but-fill. That makes the PBM adherence feeds behind Bridge, Medicaid waivers and employer premiums increasingly fictional, and the wellness-differential cases in two circuits may decide whether they can be used at all.

The national-champion deal lowered prices by tying federal supply to one company. India's WTO challenge, Novo's tariff burden and US generic semaglutide entry dates in 2033 all threaten the bargain before the Bridge expires.

The military readiness programme and employer premium conditions have given the backlash coalition concrete grievances and two state laws. The HRSA programme, which has no conditions, is attacked by conditioning advocates as waste and by the backlash as 'pacification', and its FY2033 rider is not guaranteed.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Lighter, Cheaper, Conditional: 75 Million Americans on the Pen, and Their Bones Are Starting to Show the Bill
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about seventy-five million people. The price went down, but the drug did not become free. In March 2031 the Commerce Department extended its pharmaceutical tariffs to the raw peptide and made Eli Lilly the national champion: no duty and federal loans for its new Virginia and Texas plants, in exchange for ceiling prices. The cash portal now sells semaglutide at $249 a month, tirzepatide at $299 and the starter pill at $149. Novo matched those prices and pays the duty on its Danish ingredients. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, a number nobody pays.

That June retatrutide got a higher dose, came off allocation and went on sale at $399. The two-year trial figure was thirty percent of body weight, which is the result of surgery delivered by pen. The muscled 'Charlotte build' spread down-market, but without coaching the result looks different. Trainers call it pen-thin.

Cheaper drugs did not mean freer access. Payers learned to ration through conditions instead of exclusions. The Medicare Bridge was renewed in December 2031 at $225 a month with a $50 copay, but it now drops anyone who has not lost five percent by month six, falls below eighty percent adherence or skips the annual bone scan. Seven states run Indiana-style Medicaid waivers. New federal guidance lets employers set premiums using pharmacy adherence data, and more than half of the employers that cover the drug attach conditions. The free liraglutide at community health centres is the one programme that still asks only that patients collect their refills. Critics on both sides cite it.

The bone wave arrived as numbers, not as a scandal. In September 2031 Medicare data showed hip-fracture admissions rising for the first time in twenty years. The modelled excess is about eighteen thousand a year, mostly women and mostly people who cycle on and off. The FDA moved bone-density scanning into the warnings section, and endocrinologists began prescribing bone drugs alongside the incretin as routine. In Sun City, Arizona, retirement-community gyms run waiting lists. Then in June 2032 the FDA approved semaglutide to reduce dementia risk in older adults with diabetes or heart disease. The group most frightened of losing their memory is now also the group most likely to break a hip.

The flatness people call 'the grey' stopped being a selling point and became a complaint. A retatrutide study confirmed it in 2031 and the label now says so. Nearly half of long-term users take deliberate breaks from their dose, and because coverage depends on adherence, many keep collecting refills they do not inject. That same month the FDA approved a low-dose pill for binge eating, and the ads promise to 'quiet the noise around food.'

The state now treats the drug as readiness infrastructure. The Pentagon offers tirzepatide to soldiers who fail the tape test, and about 140,000 are on it. Separations for body composition have fallen by nearly a third. Big-city police contracts cover it as well. Chaplains have forwarded about nineteen hundred religious objections.

Those objections belong to a wider counter-movement. In Grand Rapids church networks, and then in Nashville and Tulsa, 'Open Table' suppers serve full plates as fellowship. Fat-liberation supper clubs in Oakland advertise themselves as unmedicated. Tennessee and Idaho now bar employers from tying premiums to the drug. Meanwhile spirits volumes have fallen for a fourth year, snack makers keep selling brands, and gyms fill with people sent by a referral slip. From the outside the country looks leaner, calmer and more compliant.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Staff Sergeant Ramon Pruitt steps on the scale at Womack at 0630. The medic tapes his waist, reads the number aloud and taps the tablet. Green. Two more greens and he comes off the Metabolic Readiness list, though nobody comes off the pen.

He injects on Sundays: tirzepatide, issued at the pharmacy window, no copay. He skipped the last one. Kayla's sister was getting married in Raleigh, and he wanted to taste the brisket. The fill was picked up anyway. Everyone picks up.

At the motor pool Specialist Duarte is telling the bay that he filed the religious paperwork. His pastor wrote the letter. Somebody laughs, and somebody else doesn't.

At lunch Ramon eats half a burrito and wraps the rest, the way he has for a year.

His mother calls from Fayetteville at four. Her bone scan is Thursday. If she skips it, Medicare stops paying for the shot she takes for her memory. Fifty dollars a month. She broke her wrist in March getting out of the tub. 'I remember everything,' she says. 'That's the joke.'

At home Kayla has carried four casseroles in from the car for tonight's Open Table at the church. She is not on anything and hasn't been since Wren was born. She puts a full plate in front of him without a word.

Ramon eats all of it, slowly, and tastes the pepper. Then he feels the old pull for a second plate. It is loud, and he had forgotten it.

Wren, six, watches him chew.

The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived. Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

This is consistent with one-year persistence still near one-third on weekly and oral products (monthly clinic-administered MariTide runs ~60% at 12 months inside employer tracks) and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×11 + 0.33×19.5 + 0.24×29.5 + 0.23×17 = 2.2 + 6.4 + 7.1 + 3.9 ≈ 19.6. Income thirds average ~19.7, bracketing the national figure. About 19.6% of ~272M adults is ~53.3M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~26% (~13.9M, flat in absolute terms while users grew), Medicare ~21% (~11.2M), Medicaid ~6% (~3.2M), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/direct/telehealth) ~33% (~17.6M, including ~1.3M on telehealth 'calm' microdose plans), imported or counterfeit ~14% (~7.5M, up from ~5.2M). The bottom third's gain (12 → 14) comes almost entirely from gray-market product, which makes it the least stable use in the country. Adult obesity is ~33.4%. Roughly 23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and adults 65+ without CVD codes. Pediatric: ~1.2% of under-18s are on a drug, ~2.6% of 12–17s. About 0.25% of 6–11s take daily liraglutide, and new under-12 starts fell roughly a third after the Feb 2032 growth communication. About 4.5M children under 18 live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~11.2M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 11.2M × ~$235 average net/month × 12 ≈ $31.6B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up. Of that, the dementia route (~1.9M × ~$245 × 12) ≈ $5.6B. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month across 100+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–60 in markets without enforceable patents. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 50–85 and BRL 180–300. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of the world's incretin volume.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin, under review since Oct 2029, was approved Dec 2030 for chronic weight management at ~22% weight loss. It is a new product, not a new indication. Lilly's tirzepatide dementia sNDA for adults 60+ without CVD got a CRL in Jun 2031: the FDA wanted confirmatory-trial data and a fracture/EPI risk-mitigation plan, and the confirmatory trial reads out no earlier than 2033. So new_indications is 'none'. Oral semaglutide for AUD read out positive in phase 3 (2031) and was filed Jan 2032, with no decision before 2033. The monthly driver is realised through MariTide's scale-up (~4.6M users) and clinic administration inside employer tracks. No implant exists; implant programmes are in phase 1 to early phase 2 and are not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts read out phase 3 in 2031 with modest lean-mass preservation, were filed in Jul 2032 and are not approved. No oral matches tirzepatide. safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles, and is compounded in EPI patients by vitamin D/K malabsorption. The fracture data were central to the June 2031 dementia CRL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code in use; resistance-training counselling statement on retatrutide and amycretin labels.

The milder 'evenness' that most users report is now the selling point of telehealth calm plans. No randomised data; the FDA postmarketing observational study is due 2033.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language added to semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A third replication (UK CPRD, 2031) confirmed ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial recovery of faecal elastase was seen in about half of people who stopped for 12+ months. Tirzepatide data at 5+ years are emerging, with a smaller and non-significant excess so far.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling added in Mar 2031 (EPI warning; faecal elastase testing for persistent diarrhoea). EMA PRAC concluded with similar wording. Tirzepatide is under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric developmental signal arrived in 2032 (see next entry). Cycling effects on bone and pancreas remain poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density and growth postmarketing requirements continue; the interim growth analysis was published early.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~23,000 by mid-2032. In Sep 2031 CDC linked non-sterile imported vials to ~640 nontuberculous mycobacterial skin and soft-tissue infections across 22 states, plus a separate cluster of Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials at 3–5× labelled concentration (~380 ED visits for intractable vomiting and dehydration, 11 deaths in total across both clusters). Cloned serial codes now defeat the pen authentication scans. Poison-centre calls are ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert extended to named Chinese API makers. CBP seizures are up ~2.5× from 2030. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and no federal or state statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR interim analysis (n≈2,900, Jan 2032) found height velocity ~0.7 cm/year below expected in children who were prepubertal at start, with no catch-up yet observed at 24 months. A Swedish adolescent registry (started at 12–14 on semaglutide, 2023–2029) found later onset of pubertal staging in boys and an ARFID/restrictive-eating diagnosis HR of ~1.8 (absolute ~6 vs ~3.3 per 1,000 person-years). It is unclear how much of this is drug, how much caloric deficit and how much confounding by severity. Final adult height is unknown and will not be known for years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Feb 2032). The liraglutide 6–11 label was updated (Apr 2032) with growth-velocity monitoring every 6 months, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening. The AAP issued interim guidance favouring lifestyle-first for prepubertal children. No age restriction was imposed. EMA review opened.

food_and_beverage.state: About 36% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~9–11% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. Dollar sales are flat because of price and premium mix. The class split in the aisle is now a formal strategy: Kroger and Albertsons plan stores by zip-code user density, with 'GLP-1 friendly' protein bays in upper-income suburbs and value packs and private label in lower-income areas. PepsiCo and Mondelez have spun premium protein lines into separate brands. Whey prices eased as capacity came online; pea protein is still tight.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~12–13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. Losses concentrate among heavy drinkers, now also targeted by telehealth calm plans that bundle alcohol reduction. Diageo sold two US whiskey brands. Midwestern mid-sized-city bar closures continue. Non-alcoholic and functional 'calm' drinks grow but are small.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Casual-dining checks are smaller. Darden and Brinker run portion-tiered menus. QSR value menus grow in lower-income markets where gray-market users regain. Buffets are now a niche category.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Growth is in premium structured athletic wear and in tailoring for 'lifted' bodies. Resale, stretch and rental serve cyclers and regainers. Size runs are now set by store zip code at the mass retailers.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships run $250–400 a month. Budget chains sell $39 'lean-mass' add-ons. Employer metabolic tracks bundle clinic MariTide visits with InBody scans. Pediatric weight programmes lost enrolment after the growth communication, while family strength gyms gained.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is at 30%. Pharmacy trend ~+6% as flat-net deals and the MariTide PBM preference offset volume. Adherence differentials have spread to more mid-sized self-insured firms, which use clinic administration records. Part D premiums rose again in 2032, partly on incretin spend. Pediatric prior authorisation now requires growth charts.

pharma.state: Lilly, Novo, Amgen and Boehringer share the branded US market. Amgen's MariTide grew fastest on employer-track volume. Lilly's dementia growth slowed after the CRL. Novo leans on orals and the Medicare price, with semaglutide's EPI label weighing on long-term persistence. Counterfeit defence spending is in the hundreds of millions. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape reads as income, and now also as how you are paid. Lean with visible muscle means covered, scanned and coached. Thin and soft with a monthly clinic bruise means an employer track. Thin with a sallow look means cash or mail-order. Regained after 50 means lost coverage or a bad batch. Among the upper tier, a child's growth chart has joined the parent's DXA as a status document.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is the class uniform. In Charlotte and Austin the lean-mass percentage is office gossip, and 'off-drug lean' (people who stopped at goal and held it with coaching) is the newest elite boast. On the Columbus logistics corridor the plant-clinic body is thin without muscle. In Memphis and the Mississippi Delta, where gray-market use rose fastest, the visible body is the cycler, and you can read the batch history in the face. Upper-income parents in Bethesda and Plano are quietly pulling prepubertal children off liraglutide or switching to 'lifestyle-first' programmes after the growth communication. Medicaid-covered children who were added late are less likely to be monitored that closely.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Protein remains a hospitality marker. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~650 congregations and has added a youth ministry framed around the pediatric findings. School-lunch debates have shifted from accommodating medicated children to whether schools should report weight at all.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' badges remain a premium app tier. Some apps now let users tag 'on a calm plan'. Couples negotiate around the monthly shot date, and therapists report that one partner's calm subscription is a new kind of mismatch: one person finds the other flat and is told the flatness is something they pay for.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite and craving are noise that a subscription manages. In lower-income communities appetite signals lost access, or is defended as pride. The counter-movement remains split. Unmuted argues about class and the calm industry, the MAHA wing has seized on the children's growth data, and fat-acceptance revivalists stay apart from both.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. About 1.3M people pay for telehealth 'calm' and 'focus' plans: low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, $149–199 a month through TrumpRx-priced fills plus a $39–59 platform fee. They are buying the mild evenness most users report, and the anhedonia rate among them at low doses is unknown.
interior_life.framing: Telehealth platforms sell it as a feature: 'quiet the noise', 'craving-free focus', 'calm you can schedule'. Manufacturers avoid those words and say 'food noise'. HR still calls it steadiness. Clinicians call it a dose-related side effect. Unmuted calls it a sedative sold back to the people it was first prescribed to.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~5.6M employees are in adherence-verified tracks, ~3.9M of them on clinic-administered MariTide. Shift-lead promotions in Columbus-corridor logistics and national call centres informally favour enrollees. In upper-tier firms nobody monitors anything; staff buy calm plans themselves and list 'focus protocol' beside sleep tracking. The two EEOC ADA charges remain unresolved at the end of 2032.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has competition from 'off' memoir: accounts of stopping and feeling everything return. Unmuted off nights run in Detroit, Baltimore and now Memphis. Sportsbook wagering per active account is down again in insured suburbs. Streaming platforms report calm-plan subscribers favour slow 'ambient' series, and some marketers now target that segment.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The monthly shot date organises couples' calendars. Desire mismatch is the most common presenting complaint at some couples' practices. Therapists see more 'parallel lives' and a new pattern: partners who take a calm plan to cope with the other's flatness.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The adherence-premium coalition remains stalled and no state acted. The live political argument moved to children, where MAHA-aligned legislators hold hearings on the growth data without passing bills, and to calm marketing, where FDA untitled letters produced headlines but no rules. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Medicated and regained voters are increasingly sorted by zip code.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive. FDA approved amycretin, issued a CRL on the dementia extension, added EPI and micronutrient labelling to semaglutide, issued the pediatric growth communication and label update, and sent untitled letters over calm-plan marketing without enforcement. No state legislature or agency acted, Illinois's ban is still the only one, and Congress created no coverage, mandate or premium rule.

state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. Clinic administration records for monthly injections, PBM fills and telehealth app logs flow to wellness vendors under consent. Telehealth calm platforms collect mood check-ins and sell de-identified 'focus' cohorts to employer-benefit brokers. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT still has not ruled on off-label alcohol-reduction use, or now calm-plan use, among commercial drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume. US–India talks still list CBP mail enforcement without agreement. The FDA named Chinese API makers in the 2031 import-alert extension, and Beijing protested. The US cash-to-Indian-generic price gap is ~40–50×.

open_tensions: Children who started incretins before puberty are growing ~0.7 cm a year more slowly, and no one knows their final adult height. The label now says measure them, not stop, and new starts fell mostly in the households most able to monitor.

Calm is now a product. 1.3 million people buy the mild blunting that the anhedonia cohort counts as harm at higher doses. Regulators have sent letters and nothing more, and employers are starting to buy 'focus' cohorts.

7.5 million Americans take mail-order or counterfeit product, and the bottom third's rising use rests on vials that infected hundreds and overdosed hundreds more in 2031. Each bad batch converts users into regainers.

The dementia CRL pushed prevention-minded 60-year-olds toward cash and gray channels, the group with the highest fracture and EPI exposure, while Part D premiums keep rising on incretin spend under the existing label.

prose.headline: Calm, Sold Monthly: America Buys a Quieter Mind as Its Medicated Children Start Coming Up Short
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, roughly fifty-three million people, and nearly three in ten have tried one. The number rose by two points in two years, about as fast as the cheapest channels allowed. Who pays changed faster. Only 30 percent of employers still cover the drugs for weight loss. Most that remain use monitored metabolic tracks, where a nurse at the plant clinic gives a monthly shot of Amgen's MariTide and the record goes straight to the wellness vendor. Five and a half million workers sit in those programmes. Their premiums are lower if the record is complete.

Prices fell the way manufacturers chose. In 2031 Amgen cut MariTide to $249 a month in cash and won preferred status with the benefit managers. Novo and Lilly matched within weeks, bringing maintenance prices in the government's cash channel down to $199 for the Wegovy pill and below $300 for the injectables. Starting pills are still $149. The $1,349 list price is still on the box. Amycretin, approved at the end of 2030, joined the formularies behind prior authorisation.

The newest market is not for weight at all. In March 2031 a telehealth company began selling Quiet, a low-dose semaglutide subscription promising calm and focus without cravings, and within a year more than a million people subscribed to it or its imitators. The FDA sent letters and took no further action. The pills are legal and prescribed, and the advertising carefully says 'noise' and never 'anxiety'. The cohort that counts one heavy user in thirteen losing a real share of pleasure has not studied people on low doses. The subscribers are mostly salaried, mostly urban and mostly sure it is working.

The drug did not get the new use that mattered most. In June 2031 the FDA declined to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to older adults without heart disease, citing hip fractures and the pancreatic finding that by then had its own warning on semaglutide's label. Many of those people buy it anyway, for cash or by mail.

The mail is heavier than before. About seven and a half million Americans now use Indian vials, Chinese tirzepatide copies or counterfeit pens with cloned serial codes. In 2031 non-sterile vials gave hundreds of people mycobacterial skin infections. Other vials held three to five times the labelled dose and sent hundreds more to emergency rooms. Eleven people died. Seizures more than doubled, and the packages kept coming. Almost all of the bottom third's new users came through this channel, and they stop most abruptly.

In February 2032 the children's numbers arrived. An early look at the growth study attached to liraglutide's approval for six-to-eleven-year-olds found that children who started before puberty were growing about seven-tenths of a centimetre a year more slowly than expected. A Swedish registry linked early teenage semaglutide to later puberty in boys and more restrictive eating. The FDA told doctors to measure height every six months and screen for eating disorders. It did not tell them to stop. Some parents in Bethesda and Plano took their children off quietly. In families who came to the drug late, through Medicaid, fewer people are watching the chart.

The sorting of bodies continues. In Charlotte and Austin the prized body is lifted and scanned, and the newest boast is having stopped at goal and held it with a coach. Along the Columbus freight corridor the body is thin and soft and bruised once a month at the clinic. In Memphis, where gray-market use rose fastest, the visible body is the cycler's. No state acted, Congress did nothing and the complaints at the EEOC remain undecided. From a distance the country looks calmer. Some of that calm is a subscription.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Okafor clocks in at 5:52 at the distribution centre in Groveport, Ohio, eight minutes early, because the third Tuesday is clinic day. The nurse calls her name at 10:15. Left thigh this month. A scan of her badge, the MariTide pen, a sticker on her wellness card. Her premium stays at the track rate, ninety-one dollars a pay period less than Marisol's on the next line, who didn't enroll.

She eats half a turkey wrap at lunch and puts the other half in her locker for later. She won't want it later.

At four she picks up Ayo, ten, from school and drives him to the pediatric endocrinologist in Dublin. He's been on generic liraglutide for two years, a daily pen in the bathroom drawer next to her old one. The nurse measures him twice. The doctor turns the screen toward her: the curve and the dotted line under it. Not alarming, she says. We'll check again in six months. There's a handout, three pages, from the FDA.

In the parking lot Dana reads the first paragraph and folds it into her purse.

Her sister texts from Memphis: a photo of a vial with Hindi on the label and a question mark. Dana types don't, deletes it, and types is it from the same guy?

At home Ayo asks if he has to keep taking it. She says she'll ask his dad. He doesn't eat his rice.

After he's asleep she scrolls past an ad for Quiet: a woman on a balcony, eyes closed, Calm you can schedule. Dana closes the app. She feels fine. She feels, she thinks, about the same as always.

Eligibility is BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity. The negotiated rate stays at $199/month, the $50 beneficiary copay is unchanged, and the counselling visit is kept. Medicare pays 18.8% of fills ≈ 12.8M users (11.6M aged 65+ plus ≈1.2M disabled under-65): ≈6.0M diabetes and ≈6.8M obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 6.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $16.2B gross, of which beneficiaries pay 6.8M × $50 × 12 ≈ $4.1B, leaving ≈$12.2B to the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 12.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $30.6B gross. Medicaid: the federal match rises to 90% for anti-obesity medication in states that adopt the CMS 'continuation standard'. 31 states plus DC have adopted it. Medicaid pays 15.0% of fills ≈ 10.2M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $24.4B gross before supplemental rebates. CBO score for 2032–41 ≈ $190B: Medicare obesity net ≈ $14B/yr average × 10 = $140B, plus the Medicaid enhanced-match increment ≈ $5B/yr × 10 = $50B. Medicare is now the largest single purchaser of incretins in the US.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 90+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, plus generic oral semaglutide and the first liraglutide–semaglutide combination generics. China: domestic generic semaglutide and early tirzepatide copies, and Chinese API still underlies most of the global gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 55–85/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. In the US, semaglutide ANDA settlements (Sep 2031) set generic entry for 2033, and tirzepatide exclusivity runs later.

HHS–manufacturer talks for a 2032 cut collapsed in late 2031: manufacturers cited the Section 232 tariff cost, retatrutide supply allocation and guaranteed public volume, and the government did not press with generic entry already settled for 2033. Prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–279 on the federal direct portal (launched as TrumpRx), orals $149–199, retatrutide $399 direct and $1,499 list, amycretin $449 direct at launch. Payer mix of ≈68.0M users: commercial 40.7% (27.7M), Medicare 18.8% (12.8M), Medicaid 15.0% (10.2M), cash/direct 19.9% (13.5M, including ≈3.5M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers), imported/counterfeit 5.6% (3.8M); sum 68.0M = 100%. Imports fell as a share because public coverage absorbed low-income users, but grew in absolute number among the uninsured, people in non-adopting states, and users cut off by gating. ≈75% of covering employers use outcome-gated designs. drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple_agonist_30pct driver is met by an existing product in a new form. In Feb 2031 FDA approved a 12 mg retatrutide maintenance dose on TRIUMPH extension data showing 30.1% mean loss at 104 weeks. Approval required DEXA at baseline and every 12 months and a lean-mass statement in the label. Lilly put the 12 mg pen on allocation through most of 2031–32. Amycretin, under review at the start, was approved Mar 2031 for chronic weight management, the same indication, so it adds no new indication. MariTide (filed Apr 2030): FDA extended the review in 2031 to require 72-week DEXA data, and a decision is expected 2033. Survodutide resubmitted in 2031, with a PDUFA date in early 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing, and lean-mass-sparing agents are the most watched gap in the pipeline. Smoking-cessation trial with SHAPS endpoints is enrolling. No new indication this step. Incretin market ≈$170B in 2032: US ≈$145B (≈64M paying users × ≈$190 average net × 12), ex-US ≈$27B and eroding.

food_and_beverage.state: With a quarter of adults on the drug, US salty-snack volume falls ~4% a year and confectionery ~5%. Sugary-drink volume is down again. Two large packaged-food groups sold off candy portfolios to private equity in 2031–32. 'Bone-forward' fortified dairy and protein lines lead growth, and Part D counselling templates send customers to them. Grocers' 'on-plan' aisles are standard.

alcohol.state: Fifth straight year of US spirits volume decline. Beer is down too, and 'calm' subscribers have replaced the weeknight glass. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' premium formats hold. Tobacco and vape volumes are falling faster than pre-2028 trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down, and spend per cover is down ~8–10% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced protein bowls and half portions are the default. Value buffets keep closing. 'No-gram' heritage rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston are still busy, and chains now copy them as weekend 'full table' nights.

apparel.state: Size churn continues in both directions with gating drop-offs and bone pauses. Rental and resale subscriptions sized for cycling are growing. Mid-market brands cut plus inventory again, and specialists stay stable.

fitness.state: Growing. 'Prescribed lifting' is a Medicare Advantage line item, and DEXA-plus-coaching chains are expanding into strip malls. Mobile DEXA vans are booked for months. The binding constraint is staff qualified for older lifters.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is up to 66% and ~75% of it is gated. Employers shifted retirees and some over-65 workers to Medicare's new benefit. Pharmacy trend is ~+7% on volume at flat price. Bone and fall costs now land partly on Medicare Part A and Medicare Advantage. Life insurers dropped GLP-1 disclosure penalties, and one now asks applicants with BMI ≥30 why they are not treated.

pharma.state: Volume rose about 70% at flat prices. Lilly dominates through retatrutide 12 mg, tirzepatide and Foundayo. Novo holds Medicare semaglutide share and its new amycretin franchise, and settled US generic entry for 2033. Bone-agent and DEXA makers are still winners. Indian and Chinese generic makers win abroad and wait for 2033.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Normalised. Among insured adults over 40, being on the drug is as unremarkable as a statin, and being off needs a reason: 'my DEXA', 'bone pause', 'lost coverage', or 'by conviction'. Visible regain is read as being dropped from a gated plan. The thin-armed forward stoop is a recognised look in over-60s, and trained shoulders signal a well-run regimen.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use levels are narrowing (bottom third 21% against top 28%), but the quality of care is widening. Top-third users run 12 mg retatrutide or amycretin with coaching, DEXA on schedule and antiresorptives. Bottom-third users are on Medicaid continuation standards with pharmacy-kiosk weigh-ins and 4-month DEXA waits, or on imported pens with no scan. In Dayton, Tulsa and Phoenix the waiting room for the mobile DEXA van is a new social space.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm. Hosts plan by default for 'on' guests and treat 'off' guests as a special case, like an allergy. Sunday 'full-table' dinners, church potlucks and no-gram rooms persist as deliberate heritage, now smaller in relative terms.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps add an optional on/off/pausing field. 'Unmedicated' persists as a niche identity filter. Advice columns now field complaints about a partner who refuses to start, which inverts the 2030 complaint.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and quietly assumed to be managed. The 2030 backlash coalition (Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, Tulsa–Dallas 'appetite is a gift' congregations, natural-supplement influencers, disability advocates) has not shrunk in absolute numbers but is proportionally smaller. Its remaining unity is against the continuation standard, which it calls 'weigh-in welfare'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Final retatrutide postmarketing SHAPS data: ~12% of 12 mg users cross a clinically meaningful threshold versus ~5% of comparators, observational and dose-dependent. With roughly 6–7M Americans on top-dose triple or dual regimens, that implies on the order of 400–500k excess cases of clinically meaningful anhedonia if the association is causal. The ≈3.5M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers on low-dose orals are unmeasured apart from vendor surveys.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, side effect in clinic. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' still cost $149–199/month, sell 'calm' and 'focus' freely, and under FTC orders may no longer claim to treat anxiety. Prescribers say 'reward modulation'. Users call the bad version 'the grey', and normalisation makes it something people mention with a shrug.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The 2032 catalogue update of a major HR benefits platform lists 'focus' subscriptions beside meditation apps, so lifestyle-account reimbursement is now routine at large white-collar employers. Fleets, call centres and warehouses favour continuous use. Sales, hospitality and creative workers still dose down before pitches and service peaks. Unions bargain over gated-plan data, and some contracts now copy the CMS bone-pause exemption.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' still sells in Nashville and on comedy tours, but it has become a niche. Mass-market pop critics talk about a 'grey era' of mid-tempo records. Spicy food, loud venues, escape rooms and extreme sports keep growing among users looking for stronger stimulus.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely screen for dose and subscriptions. Dose-holiday weekends are common enough that pharmacies stock 'restart' anti-nausea packs. Couples counselling now often deals with one partner on 'Quiet' and the other off.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Politics is about who pays and on what terms. The continuation standard is the fight: Republicans frame it as accountability, many Democrats as necessary stewardship, and disability and backlash groups as surveillance. 'Calm voter' turnout effects remain unpublished speculation. Senior advocacy groups now lobby on DEXA capacity.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding: it requires DEXA in every filing, put body-composition monitoring into the 12 mg retatrutide and amycretin labels, and extended MariTide's review. Import enforcement is selective, with no individual prosecutions and no importation law. FTC acts on claims through consent orders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Public expansion: a permanent Part D obesity benefit at $199 with a $50 copay from Jan 2032, and 90% federal match for state Medicaid programmes that adopt the continuation standard (31 states plus DC). No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard (final rule Dec 2031) applies to Part D obesity users and enhanced-match Medicaid. Its terms: ≥80% PDC from pharmacy claims; a verified weight every 6 months via pharmacy kiosks or a connected scale; ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override; annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users; and a 90-day 'bone pause' code. Missing two verifications suspends coverage for 6 months, which is softer than Indiana and Arkansas, whose 12-month rules continue. Private gating covers ~75% of employer plans without a pause exemption. BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to 30% of premium continue.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets add DEXA for drivers over 55. Army accession policy is still contested; the Air Force allows waivers for applicants stable for 12 months.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world. A US–India trade framework (2032) lists 'pharmaceutical parcel cooperation' without legalising import. Section 232 tariffs remain and are cited by manufacturers as a reason prices stalled. Lilly's 12 mg allocation is blamed on fill-finish capacity in North Carolina and Ireland.

open_tensions: The CMS continuation standard requires annual DEXA for long-term older users while scanner capacity runs 12–20 weeks behind. Medicare's bone-pause code protects paused seniors, but the ~75% of gated employer plans have no such exemption, so a 58-year-old following the same guidance can lose coverage her mother keeps.

Medicare is now the largest payer at exactly the age where the bone and fall harms concentrate. The drug is billed to Part D, while the fractures, falls and sarcopenia rehabilitation are billed to Part A and Medicare Advantage. No CBO score includes the second set of costs.

Prices stalled with US generic semaglutide fixed for 2033. Meanwhile ≈3.8M Americans inject imported or counterfeit product at $5–30, and Congress has neither legalised import nor sealed the mail. The 2033 cliff will reprice the whole public bill.

About 3.5M people without obesity buy reward modulation as 'focus' through employer catalogues, while the best data call it a dose-dependent harm in about one in eight top-dose users. Normalisation is making the question harder to raise, not easier.

prose.headline: Off It? Explain Yourself. Medicare Now Pays for the Pen, and Wants to See Your Bones First
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, and nobody remarks on it. What people remark on is being off. Off has a short list of acceptable reasons: a bone pause, a lost plan, a scan you could not get. Saying you simply chose not to take it still draws a look in a suburban kitchen in Ohio or Arizona.

The jump from one in seven did not come from cheaper drugs. Prices stopped falling. The $199 pen of the 2029 deal is still $199, because the manufacturers had guaranteed public volume, a tariff to point to and a generic date that was already settled. When Novo fixed US generic semaglutide entry for 2033, the government stopped pushing for more. What changed was the payer. In July 2031 Congress used a reconciliation bill to turn the Medicare Bridge into a permanent Part D benefit at the same $199 rate and $50 copay. It also offered states a ninety-percent federal match to cover the drugs in Medicaid. Thirty-one states and Washington, D.C. accepted. Medicare is now the largest buyer of incretins in the country. The share of Americans over sixty-five on the drug has doubled, and the bottom income third is on it at nearly twice its 2030 rate.

The money came with conditions. Under the CMS continuation standard, pharmacy claims track adherence, a kiosk by the blood-pressure cuff records a verified weight every six months, and anyone who has not lost five percent by month six needs a clinician to vouch for them. Long-term users over sixty-five must have a bone-density scan every year. There is one concession to the bone data: a 'pause' code that lets a doctor take someone off for ninety days without losing coverage. Employer plans, three-quarters of which are gated, mostly have no such code. A daughter can lose her coverage for doing exactly what her mother's Medicare plan allows.

The bone problem keeps growing because the older population on the drug keeps growing. A Medicare claims analysis this spring put the excess at about eleven and a half thousand hip fractures a year, against three hundred thousand in all, plus a tail of vertebral fractures among women in their fifties who have cycled on and off several times. Scans are scarce. Across the Sun Belt the wait for a DEXA appointment runs to four or five months. Mobile scanners park outside churches and gyms, and their waiting areas have become a place where retirees talk. The drug is billed to Part D, and the broken hips are billed to Part A. Nobody's budget score shows both.

The strongest weight-loss drug is now a pen. A 12-milligram dose of Lilly's triple agonist reaches about thirty percent average loss. Its label requires body scans, and supply has been rationed for most of its first year. Novo's amycretin arrived beside it. Neither drug added a new indication. The FDA asked for more bone data on every filing it saw.

The quieting effect is still for sale. About three and a half million people with no weight problem pay $149 a month for 'Quiet' or 'Even' to take the edge off, and since August the big HR benefits platforms list these alongside meditation apps. The FTC stopped the anxiety claims, but 'calm' and 'focus' are still allowed. The best observational data suggest roughly one top-dose user in eight loses a measurable capacity for pleasure. Because so many people take the drug, that has become something people mention in passing.

The counter-movement is still there: Atlanta's body-sovereignty collectives, the Tulsa churches, the berberine sellers, the disability lawyers. They now gather mostly against what they call weigh-in welfare. Nearly four million Americans still inject pens from Hyderabad or Shenzhen. Every institution is waiting for 2033.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marlene Pruitt, sixty-seven, steps onto the kiosk at the Kroger pharmacy in Kettering at 7:40, before the line forms. Shoes off, as the sign says. The screen thanks her, shows 171.4, and turns green. A receipt prints: CONTINUATION VERIFIED — NEXT DUE 02/2033.

She pays the fifty dollars for a month of Zepbound and asks again about the scan. The pharmacist checks. The DEXA van is at Southbrook Christian on the fourteenth of January. Her annual scan was due in November. 'Dr. Iyer filed the capacity extension,' he says. 'You're fine.' Marlene has heard 'you're fine' before.

At the Y, the instructor of Strong Bones 65 calls her 'Miss Marlene' and hands her the twelve-pound kettlebell instead of the ten. Three of the eight women in the class are on bone pauses. One of them, Gwen, has the stoop already. Nobody mentions it. Afterward Gwen says her son's plan at the distribution centre dropped him in October for two missed weigh-ins. He was working doubles. He's ordering from India now. 'They come in a padded envelope,' Gwen says. 'He checks the hologram.'

At dinner her daughter-in-law Keisha pushes chicken around her plate and says the 'Even' subscription her firm pays for has made her stop fighting with Darnell, and she means it as good news. Darnell laughs a beat late.

Marlene's granddaughter, nine, asks why Grandma eats the meat first. 'For my bones,' Marlene says. The girl nods. Everyone she knows eats like that.
